author: Ted Black
title: High school female athletes honored for spring sports - NewsBreak
text:
By Ted Black ,
21 hours ago
Southern Maryland Athletic Conference female athletes exceled throughout the spring season and the following four ascended to the head of the class in their particular sport.
Girls lacrosse — Alaina “Ally” Burks, Leonardtown senior
Not only was Alaina “Ally” Burks a prominent three-sport athlete with the Raiders as a member of the girls soccer, girls basketball and girls lacrosse teams, she ascended to the head of the class in the latter. Burks led the Raiders with 555 goals, including four in a losing cause last month when Leonardtown fell to Urbana 8-6 in the Maryland 4A State Championship game at Stevenson University. Leonardtown goalie Madison Buehler, Northern senior Mia Barber, Huntingtown senior Anya Bortchevsky, La Plata senior twins Addison Mudd and Kinsey Mudd and sophomore Ruby Tharaldson also were solid all season.
Softball — Rachael Howell, Huntingtown senior, and Melody Russell, Northern senior
While the tandem of Rachael Howell and Melody Russell competed for rival schools, both were instrumental in leading their squads to their respective state championships last spring. Howell emerged as the ace of the Hurricanes staff after yielding that role to former Huntingtown standout hurler Jordyn Greever the three previous seasons. Howell suffered only one setback all spring — coincidentally to eventual 3A state champion Northern — then later blanked Middletown 1-0 in the 2A state semifinals and later defeated Mt Hebron 3-1 in the state finals at the University of Maryland. Russell batted leadoff and player center field for the Patriots and was a genuine spark plug for the 3A State champions all season. The Barton College recruit batted .585 (41 for 71) with 25 walks, scored 50 runs, stole 32 bases and also smacked two home runs. Huntingtown first baseman Madalee Hunley, Chopticon pitcher Karllie Nelson and Patriots’ infielders Maddie Jewett and twins Brooke MacAulay and Delaney MacAulay were also stellar all season. St. Mary’s Ryken senior catcher Ava Chadwick shared WCAC player of the year honors.
Tennis — Lucy Staley, Huntingtown senior
Throughout her high school career with the Hurricanes, Lucy Staley was part of four SMAC champions, three region titles and also made two appearances in the state finals while playing doubles alongside former standout Bella White. This past spring Staley and Huntingtown sophomore Uwem Inyanga also enjoyed ample success in the Mixed Doubles and they attained the highest finish among SMAC players by placing third in the Maryland state tournament. They rebounded from a setback to the eventual state champs to prevail in the consolation match to earn the bronze. La Plata’s Taylor Carter and Joyce Kang had a solid season in girls’ doubles while Northern senior Ahvlee Reist and McDonough senior Addyson Jarmuscz also enjoyed a solid spring in singles.
Track and field — Aiyanna Smalley, Patuxent senior, and Evagellia Lilly Okwuosa, Lackey junior
Throughout the postseason a pair of female athletes from two of the smaller schools in the Southern Maryland Athletic Conference came up big as both Aiyanna Smalley and Evagellia Lilly Okwuosa recorded a pair of first-place performances at the Maryland State Track & Field Championships at Morgan State University. Smalley captured both the 1A girls high jump (5-04) and also took the long jump (16-09.50). Okwuosa captured the 2A title in the long jump (18-01.50) and triple jump (38-07.50). McDonough sophomore Olivia St. Vil, Chopticon senior Allison Sonon, Northern senior Brooke Ratliff, Huntingtown junior Kaitlyn Tempera and Calvert freshman Leah Rannacher all performed superbly throughout the spring as well. Northern senior Ahvlee Reist, McDonough senior Addyson Jarmusz and La Plata junior Taylor Carter also had solid spring seasons at the net.
